public_rationale: Fortune reported (e1) that on 29 October 2024 Musk predicted AI would be able to do anything a human can do within the next year or two. Marcus's implied forecast is that this will not happen. Under the contract, the window ends on 30 October 2026, two days after the evaluation date. The contract allows early contradiction only if credible evidence shows an AI system matching humans on essentially all tasks. The packet has no such evidence. In July 2026 the Center for AI Safety reported (e2) that the best automation rate on the Remote Labor Index was 15.8%. It also said AIs still fell short of professional quality on most projects. That does not meet the early-contradiction rule. Under the contract, support can only be assessed after the deadline.
limitations: The deadline falls after the evaluation date.
The Remote Labor Index covers remote digital work only, not physical tasks.
The packet contains no evaluations from the last months before the deadline.

statement.document_title: An epidemic of weirdly precise AI butt facts

from_speaker: "able to do anything that any human can do"
My offer to bet him a million dollars ... stands
our_interpretation: Marcus's implied forecast: by two years after Musk's 2024-10-29 remark, no AI will be able to do anything any human can do.
Deadline: the latest reasonable end of 'within the next year or two' is two years after the post, 2026-10-30.
The bet offer itself is not checkable. Only the implied forecast is graded.

Early resolution rule: the forecast is contradicted early if, before the deadline, credible evaluations show an AI system able to do essentially any task a human can do, including physical and long-horizon work. It can be supported only once the deadline passes.
criteria.support_condition: At 2026-10-30, AI systems still cannot do many tasks humans can do, as shown by public capability evaluations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: By 2026-10-30, credible evidence shows an AI system that can do anything any human can do.
